Split clones whose cells disagree with the clone state on a segment

Source: R/clones_discovery.R
split_disagree.Rd

Targeted split pass of caller_tumour() (split_pass = "disagree"). Allele-driven discovery can put cells that share a haplotype imbalance but differ by one copy in one clone (e.g. a chr21 loss subclone inside a chr21 CN-LOH clone; a chr21 3:0 / 4:0 LOH-gain subclone inside a 2:1 clone, fitted 3:1). For each clone with >= 2 min_size members and each of its non-neutral segments (ploidy 2, >= split_min_len; the copy-neutral 2:0 included), every member is scored on the discovery halves (win_disc, votes_disc) under the clone state and under each alternative of split_alt_states(). Depth: the cell's segment log2 ratio, centred on the members' median (the clone state; clone profiles are relative to the clone baseline), in units of its sd_null scaled to the half depth and inflated by the members' own robust spread, t density at c * log2(cn / cn_state) (clone c from par). Alleles: the cell's votes oriented by the clone's leave-one-out pseudobulk, beta-binomial at 0.5 + a_eff (f - 0.5), a_eff = the attenuation of the members' pooled oriented fraction. The contradiction of a segment is the fraction of members whose best state is not the clone state; its noise floor is the same fraction on data simulated under the clone state at each cell's SD and vote count (5 replicates). The alternative is the state with the largest excess preference over its noise floor. A segment is a candidate when the contradiction is >= 10 % and exceeds its noise floor by >= split_min_excess, and a two-means split of the per-cell log-likelihood difference (alternative - clone state) has both parts >= max(min_size, small_clone, 10 %) and a separation >= split_sep. Candidates are ranked by the excess contradiction (not by separation: the 8q amplicon's depth spread is unimodal and wide) over all clones; up to split_cand per clone are tested, at most one split per clone and split_max splits in all. A candidate is applied when (1) the permutation split test (split_test(), budget q) on the test halves, restricted to the cdata regions the segment overlaps (>= 80 %, else >= 50 % of the shorter of the two; depth + allele), says different, and (2) the two parts re-fitted on the test halves (clone_profiles(), fit_states, segment_clone()) differ on the segment (copy number or major fraction, clone_state_distance() with min_df = 0.01, min_dcn = 1 as the caller's same-state merge) over >= max(same_dist, half the segment), with the re-fitted states at >= 1 copy, both within 2 and one within 1 copies (total) of the clone state (the clone state of a mixture is an average: e.g. a fitted 4:1 / 3:1 clone that is a mix of 2:1 and 3:0 / 4:0 cells).

Usage

split_disagree(
  members,
  segments,
  par,
  inp,
  win_disc,
  votes_disc,
  cdata,
  win_test = NULL,
  votes_test = NULL,
  ref_cells = character(),
  fit_states = NULL,
  opts = clone_defaults(),
  params = caller_defaults(),
  seed = 1,
  frac = 0.5
)

Arguments

members

data.table cell, clone (confident members)

segments

segments table of the members' clones

par

data.table clone, c, a (fit_clone_states() par)

inp

scn_features list or clone_input (regions, atoms, cells, features for sd_null, tpar, rho)

win_disc, votes_disc

discovery halves of the window depth and the votes (split_win(), split_votes())

cdata

contrast_data() of the test halves

win_test, votes_test

test halves for the re-fit (default: the full inp$win / inp$votes)

ref_cells

depth reference cells of the re-fit (used with >= min_ref cells)

fit_states

optional replacement of fit_clone_states() (function(profile, grid))

opts

clone_defaults() (min_size, split_sep, split_max, split_cand, split_min_len, split_min_df, split_min_excess, q, n_perm, max_cells, depth_delta, same_dist, small_clone, size_small, min_ref, p_switch, min_win, min_llr)

params

caller_defaults() (sd_floor, eps)

seed

RNG seed

frac

fraction of the counts in the discovery half

Value

list(members = relabelled members (split clones get suffixes a / b, b = the part that prefers the alternative), tests = one row per candidate: clone, region, chrom, start, end, state, alt, n, contra (fraction of members whose best state differs from the clone's), contra_null (its noise floor), excess, contra_alt / contra_alt_null (the same for the alternative), a_eff, infl (depth SD inflation), sep, n_a, n_b, d_a, d_b (mean log-likelihood difference per part), outcome, rank, stat, thr, n_perm, p (permutation p of the test-half split test), differ, state_a, state_b (re-fitted states at the segment midpoint), dist_bp, split), cells_b = named list of the moved cells per applied split (names = the b clones), sets = per candidate (rows of tests) the proposed parts list(a, b)
